why: The authors released everything the match target needs: the full implementation lives in robust_estim_sbm.ipynb (the paper's Code + Experiments sections), the synthetic SBM graph is generated in-code from the published parameters, and the jazz/polbooks/polblogs CSVs are already in the repo. There are no weights and no external downloads. The only work is mechanical: extract the code cells out of the 17 MB notebook (it has no .py files) and execute just the single-run synthetic experiment cell for C1 rather than the whole notebook. Runtime is the real risk: the paper reports ~14 min for that run on a 2.7 GHz dual-core, and our budget is ~20 min total including install.
entrypoints: robust_estim_sbm.ipynb — cells in the 'Code' section (SubSearch S.A., spectral clustering/plug-in estimator, cost c(S), pruning + filtering baselines)

robust_estim_sbm.ipynb — the 'Experiments' cell that instantiates the single-run synthetic config (n=200, K=2, Γ11=Γ22=0.65, Γ12=0.35, γ=0.3, |S|=140, L_t=60, T0=2.25, seed=12345, cooling 0.99, t_max=1000, t_tol=25) and calls run()
missing_artifacts: no .py modules — all logic must be lifted out of the notebook (nbconvert / json cell extraction)
no saved results/pickle artifacts of the reported run (must be regenerated)

no explicit statement of the graph-generation RNG seed for the C1 instance beyond the S.A. seed 12345 — exact 0.05 hinges on it; if the notebook does not fix it, the number will be 0.05±0.02 on a fresh draw
blockers_seen: notebook is 17.2 MB with embedded outputs; naive `jupyter nbconvert --execute` would run every experiment (multi-run synthetic, jazz, polbooks, polblogs) and blow the budget by hours — must select only the Code section + the C1 cell

requirements.txt pins numpy==1.26.0 / scikit-learn==1.3.2 / scipy==1.13.1 / pandas==2.1.4; these do have cp312 wheels, so Python 3.12.10 is workable, but scikit-network is unpinned and may need a recent release
reported runtime (14 min) is a large fraction of the ~20 min machine budget, so the clean re-run has little headroom

feasibility.est_runtime_on_this_machine: install ~3-5 min; extracting cells ~2 min; C1 S.A. run ~8-14 min (single-threaded Python loop over t_max=1000 Metropolis steps, each a K=2 spectral clustering + SVD on a 140-node submatrix, so it will not use the 22 cores); oracle and pruning baselines <5 s. Total ~15-20 min.
feasibility.scale_down_plan: Only if the t_max=1000 chain overruns ~12 min: shorten the chain (t_max=400-500, or cooling rate 0.98) or drop t_tol to 10 to reach the low-temperature plateau sooner. Effect: the returned subgraph is slightly less converged, so sum-absolute error typically lands in 0.04-0.10 rather than exactly 0.05, and the '5 of 60 outliers' count (C7) may shift by a couple of nodes — would be reported as partially_reproduced. C2/C3/C4 baselines are seconds and can always be reproduced exactly.

compute.basis: Paper's own measurement: one simulated-annealing chain of t_max=1000 steps at ~14 min on a 2.7 GHz dual-core i5; each step is a sequential numpy/scipy SVD plus spectral clustering on a 140x140 submatrix, so the extra cores and the absence of a GPU do not change wall-clock much — the estimate is that run plus ~5 min of environment setup and cell extraction.
